extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, attorneys, agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for ordering/handling patented/abandoned files, treatment of abstracts/defensive publications as prior art, and detailed policies for conducting, recording, and scheduling interviews between applicants (or their representatives) and patent examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering of patented and abandoned files (PALM process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patented and abandoned paper files are ordered by means of a PALM video display transaction. The examiner must input PALM location code, employee number, and patent and/or application numbers. A response screen informs the examiner whether the request is accepted, accepted but stored off site, not accepted because file not located, not accepted because previous request not filled, or not accepted because number is not valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodically each day Files Repository personnel perform a PALM print transaction producing a list of accepted requests; printed record is detached when file is found and stapled to it; periodic deliveries are made to requestors. Image File Wrapper (IFW) applications are stored electronically and the electronic file is the official record (no paper wrapper to order).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery of drawings with file wrappers
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of certain older files, the drawings of patented and abandoned files, if any, are stored within their respective application file wrappers and both the file and its drawings are delivered when a file is ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because drawings and wrappers are desired not to be separated, both are delivered together. For applications in IFW, ordering/delivery of paper files is not necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of abandonment (PTOL-1432) and applicant responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Examining Corps mails a Notice of Abandonment form PTOL-1432 to the correspondence address of record in all applications which become abandoned for failure to prosecute; mere failure to receive the notice does not affect the status of abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mailing enables applicants to take action to reinstate inadvertently abandoned applications (often by petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137). If neither Office action nor notice was received and lack of diligent action is claimed, suspect a problem with correspondence address of record and promptly file a paper notifying the Office of the change of address (see MPEP §§ 402 and 601.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment received after allowance or issue fee payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipt of a letter of abandonment while an application is allowed is acknowledged by the Publishing Division. An express abandonment arriving after the issue fee has been paid will not be accepted without a showing of one of the reasons in 37 CFR 1.313(c) or a showing under 37 CFR 1.183 justifying suspension of 1.313.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 711.01 for related rules and evidentiary requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization and historical practice for Abstracts, Abbreviatures, and Defensive Publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts, abbreviatures, and Defensive Publication Program outputs are publications prepared historically (abstracts discontinued 1953, abbreviatures discontinued 1965). The Defensive Publication Program published abstracts where applicants waived enforceable patent rights (available 1968–1985) and is distinct from patent or application publication under 35 U.S.C. 122(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A defensive publication is prior art only as of its publication date. Defensive publications had special effects on entitlement to benefit of filing dates for continuations (e.g., 30-month window). Defensive Publication files are maintained in the File Information Unit; numbering systems changed over time and conversion tables exist in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of abstracts/abbreviatures/defensive publications as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts, abbreviatures, and defensive publications must be referred to as publications and are cited as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or 102(b) effective from the date of publication in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They may be used alone or in combination with other prior art in rejecting claims under 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103. Defensive publications are listed with 'U.S. Patent Documents'; abstracts and abbreviatures are listed under 'Other References' with specific citation formats provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited use of application portions underlying abstracts/abbreviatures as references
rubrics_metrics.description: An application or portion thereof from which an abstract, abbreviature or defensive publication has been prepared may be used as a reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(a), effective from the actual date of filing in the United States, only for evidence of prior knowledge of another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction limits when the underlying application text can be treated as an earlier-filed reference (i.e., primarily to support evidence of knowledge rather than full prior-art effect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'interview' for patent prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: The personal appearance of an applicant, attorney, or agent before the examiner or a telephone conversation or video conference or electronic mail between such parties presenting matters for the examiner’s consideration is considered an interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This inclusive definition covers in-person, telephonic, video, and electronic mail communications when substantive matters are presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: General interview policy and location (37 CFR 1.133)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews with examiners concerning applications and other matters pending before the Office must be conducted on Office premises and within Office hours, as designated by the examiner; interviews are not permitted at any other time or place without the Director’s authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews discussing patentability will not occur before the first Office action unless the application is a continuing/substitute application or the examiner determines the interview would advance prosecution. The examiner may require that an interview be scheduled in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written statement requirement after interview when reconsideration requested
rubrics_metrics.description: In every instance where reconsideration is requested in view of an interview with an examiner, a complete written statement of the reasons presented at the interview as warranting favorable action must be filed by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interview does not remove the necessity for replying to Office actions as specified in §§ 1.111 and 1.135.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet electronic mail restrictions for interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet e-mail shall NOT be used to conduct exchanges or communications similar to those exchanged during telephone or personal interviews unless a written authorization from the applicant or an attorney/agent of record has been given to use Internet e-mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Internet e-mail is used with authorization, a paper copy of the e-mail contents MUST be made and placed in the patent application file as required by the Federal Records Act in the same manner as an Examiner Interview Summary Form is entered (see MPEP § 502.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Video Conference Center (VCC) availability and scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO established a Video Conference Center to expedite prosecution; VCC equipment includes high-resolution document camera, direct computer input, VCR, high-speed fax. Use is available for authorized official business during normal hours and currently limited to authorized PTDL partnership locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customers wishing to use PTDL facilities should contact the examiner with two alternative dates/times. The examiner will coordinate with Office of Patent Training; video conferences must be arranged at least 3 days in advance. Use and scheduling are handled by the examiner, not by applicants contacting training staff directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling interviews and Applicant Initiated Interview Request (PTOL‑413A)
rubrics_metrics.description: An interview should normally be arranged in advance (letter, fax, e-mail, telegram, or telephone). When applicant initiates, an 'Applicant Initiated Interview Request' form (PTOL‑413A) should be submitted prior to the interview to permit examiner preparation; the form should identify participants, proposed date, interview type, and a brief description of issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of PTOL‑413A should be attached to the Interview Summary form PTOL‑413 at completion and given to the applicant. Applicants are encouraged to use PTOL‑413A but failure to submit it is not by itself grounds to deny an interview. An appointment should be kept; if circumstances prevent attendance, notify the other party immediately to allow substitute arrangements. For VCC interviews, arrange at least 3 days in advance; when a second art unit is involved, check availability of second examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone call conduct during interviews and follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: When a telephone call indicates a lengthy discussion or the examiner needs time to restudy, the call should be terminated with an agreement that the examiner will call back at a specified time. Calls originated by the examiner should be made through the Office’s telephone system even if a collect call was authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include complete telephone numbers with area code and extension on correspondence, preferably near signatures. If a call will be lengthy, schedule a callback so discussion is properly prepared and limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissibility standards for interviews (purpose and preparedness)
rubrics_metrics.description: An interview should be had only when it could serve to develop and clarify specific issues and lead to a mutual understanding and thereby advance prosecution. The attorney presenting for an interview should be fully prepared to discuss the issues raised in the Office action; if not prepared, an interview should not be permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is desirable that the attorney indicate in advance the issues to be discussed by submitting, in writing, a proposed amendment so the examiner can prepare and focus the interview. Interviews that are solely to 'sound out' the examiner (e.g., local attorney for out‑of‑town principal) should not be permitted when any agreement is conditional on the principal attorney’s acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner conduct during interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should avoid unnecessary interruptions during interviews (e.g., not take incoming calls unless emergency). They should familiarize themselves with the status/issues before interviews and should not hesitate to state that claims require further search/study or to conclude an interview when no common ground can be reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should attempt to identify issues and resolve differences during the interview as much as possible, may suggest allowable subject matter to accelerate agreement, and can make suggestions to unrepresented applicants but should limit time for such assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable length for interviews (time limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Both parties are responsible to ensure an interview is not extended beyond a reasonable period, usually not longer than 30 minutes. It is the duty of the primary examiner to see that an interview is not extended beyond a reasonable period even when not personally participating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This guideline applies to in-person, telephonic, and video interviews; time management is a shared responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after final rejection and requests following first action
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may grant one interview after final rejection (see MPEP § 713.09). Where the reply to a first complete action includes a request for an interview, telephone consultation, or video conference, or where an out‑of‑town attorney requests delay until next Washington visit (provided not beyond the date the Office action would be given), the examiner should grant the request if it appears the interview would expedite the case to a final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When agreement is reached as a result of an interview, applicant’s representative should be advised that an amendment pursuant to the agreement should be promptly submitted. If the amendment prepares the case for final action, the examiner should take the case up as special; if not, await its turn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of duplicate copy and processing of filed amendments after interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of a filed amendment may be had by hand delivery of a duplicate copy of the amendment. Although entry of amendatory matter usually requires actual presence of the original paper, examiner and technical support processing should proceed as far as practicable based on the duplicate copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extent of processing depends on the amendment; for IFW processing see IFW Manual section 3.5. Early communication of results should be made to applicant; if requested, indicate any agreement on attorney’s copy and initial/date both copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that the substance of any interview be made of record
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete written statement as to the substance of any face‑to‑face, video conference, electronic mail or telephone interview with regard to the merits of an application must be made of record in the application, whether or not an agreement was reached (see 37 CFR 1.133(b), MPEP §§ 502.03 and 713.01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.2 requires business with the Office be transacted in writing; the Office's action is based exclusively on the written record. If the record is incomplete through failure to record interview substance, the Office cannot rely exclusively on the record. The responsibility to make the substance of an interview of record lies with the applicant or the applicant’s representative, except where the examiner initiates and indicates on PTOL‑413B that the examiner will provide a written summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview Summary form PTOL‑413 and PTOL‑413B procedures and required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must complete an Interview Summary form PTOL‑413 for each interview where a matter of substance was discussed; if examiner initiated, PTOL‑413B may be used. PTOL‑413 shall be given a paper number, placed in the file, and listed on the contents list; a duplicate is given to applicant at conclusion or mailed for telephonic/email/video interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTOL‑413 records: (A) application number; (B) name of applicant; (C) name of examiner; (D) date; (E) type of interview; (F) participants; (G) whether an exhibit/demonstration shown; (H) identification of claims discussed; (I) identification of specific prior art discussed; (J) indication whether agreement reached and description; (K) signature of examiner; (L) names of other USPTO personnel present. The complete recordation should also include: (A) brief description of exhibits/demonstrations; (B) claims discussed; (C) prior art discussed; (D) principal proposed substantive amendments (unless already described); (E) general thrust of principal arguments of applicant and examiner (not verbatim); (F) other pertinent matters; (G) general results/outcome; (H) for e-mail interviews, a paper copy must be placed in the file. If applicant’s interview record is incomplete/inaccurate and bears on patentability, examiner may give applicant one month to correct the record (extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) may be granted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner review and verification of applicant interview summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s summary of what took place at the interview should be carefully checked by the examiner to determine accuracy of any argument or statement attributed to the examiner. If an inaccuracy bears directly on patentability, it should be pointed out in the next Office letter. If the record is complete and accurate, the examiner should mark 'Interview record OK' with date and initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the record is not complete/accurate, the examiner may give applicant one month to supply omission/correction to avoid abandonment; sample form paragraph (¶ 7.84) provides notice language for non-responsive amendment regarding interview record omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity when a different examiner continues examination after interview
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner who conducted the interview is transferred or resigns and another examiner continues examination, the second examiner should ascertain if any agreements were reached. Where conditions permit (absence of clear error or knowledge of other prior art), the second examiner should take a position consistent with agreements previously reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is intended to preserve the effect of interview agreements unless there is a clear basis to depart; see MPEP § 812.01 for related telephone practice in restriction/election situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited interviews and special situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in unusual situations, no interview is permitted after the brief on appeal is filed or after an application has been passed to issue. Office employees are forbidden to hold oral or written communication with an unregistered or a suspended/excluded attorney or agent regarding an application unless that attorney/agent is the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 105 for rules concerning communications with unregistered/suspended practitioners and § 713.01/713.05 for other special interview situations (e.g., Saturday interviews).
